2024 Edo Governorship Election Presidential Gubernatorial Ibrahim Masari
President Bola Tinubu’s Senior Special Assistant on Political Matters, Ibrahim Masari, has spoken out about his rift with his home-state governor, Dikko Radda of Katsina State.
In an interview with the BBC Hausa Service released on Monday morning and monitored by PREMIUM TIMES, Mr Masari addressed a controversy surrounding the police invitation of Governor Radda’s Aide-de-Camp (ADC) and Chief Security Officer (CSO), and the arrest of several political actors amid factional tensions within the Katsina State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC).
Mr Masari explained that the dispute began when some of the governor’s aides and supporters erected campaign billboards across the state featuring the governor without President Tinubu’s portrait—a move he and other federal appointees from Katsina opposed.
“We produced separate billboards, banners, and posters for the president and placed them in strategic locations,” Mr Masari said.
“Our billboards were all-inclusive, featuring the portraits of the president, the vice president, the governor, and two immediate past governors Aminu Masari and Ibrahim Shema.”
He alleged that security aides attached to the Government House orchestrated the destruction of those promotional billboards.
“I cannot confirm whether the governor was aware or not, but his aide-de-camp and the chief security officer at the Government House led thugs at night to destroy the billboards,” he stated.

“Those thugs, including some of the governor’s aides, were arrested by the police at the scene of the crime. This is the root of my problem with the governor. I disagree with the notion that the state government cannot feature the president on its campaign billboards, and we will resist anyone who attempts to separate them.”
The billboard dispute escalated into a major political flashpoint in late August 2026.
Following petitions over the vandalism of billboards displaying President Tinubu and Mr Masari across Katsina, the police summoned Governor Radda’s two senior security officers to the Force Headquarters in Abuja for questioning.
After both officers returned to their duty posts at the Katsina Government House, a political group leader, Aminu Sanda, popularly known as Aminu Nasta, and several suspected thugs were arrested in connection with the destruction of the billboards.
The state government is yet to comment on the allegations. The governor’s media aide, Ibrahim Kaula, could not be reached immediately through his known phone number Monday morning to comment on the allegations.
Despite the friction over party structures and campaign branding, Mr Masari maintained that he still supports Governor Radda’s administration and praised his governance record since assuming office in May 2023.
“Dikko Radda has an excellent record of performance; his achievements are noticeable, and even his detractors can attest to his work, and I have never regretted my support for the governor,” Mr Masari said.
Mr Masari also dismissed widespread allegations that he engineered the removal of former Minister of Housing and Urban Development, Ahmed Dangiwa—a known ally of the Katsina political establishment—and his replacement with his own close associate, Muttaka Rabe.
“God and President Tinubu will bear me witness that I never influenced the removal of the minister.
“All the allegations against me are an injustice to my person, and God will vindicate me”, Mr Masari said in the interview anchored by Rabi’atu Runka.
